classification.difficultyReason: Translate the bearings onto the supplied triangle, use the reverse bearing to justify the right angle, then select cosine to find AC. The parts scaffold the geometry; the separate travel-time calculation requires a routine conversion to hours and minutes.

content.prompt:
Checkpoint $C$ is due east of Checkpoint $A$.
The bearing of Checkpoint $B$ from Checkpoint $A$ is N$22^\circ$E and the bearing of Checkpoint $C$ from Checkpoint $B$ is S$68^\circ$E.
The distance between Checkpoint $A$ and Checkpoint $B$ is 42 kilometres.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Label the diagram and explain why $\angle ABC=90^\circ$.

spec.description: Unfilled triangle with A lower left, B above and to the right of A, C lower right, horizontal AC and a separate upward north arrow. Only vertex labels and N are supplied.
spec.mathematics: The schematic coordinates follow the stated bearings: AB points N22°E, BC points S68°E, and C lies due east of A. No numerical coordinate values are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Question figure contains no distances, bearing arcs, angle values or right-angle marker.

answer.short: $AB=42\text{ km}$, $\angle BAC=68^\circ$ and $\angle BCA=22^\circ$. At $B$, $BA$ is S$22^\circ$W and $BC$ is S$68^\circ$E, so $\angle ABC=22^\circ+68^\circ=90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Label $AB=42\text{ km}$, the bearing of $B$ from $A$ as N$22^\circ$E, and the bearing of $C$ from $B$ as S$68^\circ$E.
The reverse bearing of $A$ from $B$ is S$22^\circ$W. The south direction at $B$ lies between $BA$ and $BC$, so
$$\begin{aligned}\angle ABC&=22^\circ+68^\circ\\&=90^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
Since $AC$ is due east,
$$\begin{aligned}\angle BAC&=90^\circ-22^\circ\\&=68^\circ,\\\angle BCA&=180^\circ-90^\circ-68^\circ\\&=22^\circ.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Completed triangle with AB labelled 42 km, north directions at A and B, the south reference at B, bearing reference angles, interior angles and a right-angle square at B.
spec.mathematics: BA is S22°W and BC is S68°E, giving 22°+68°=90° at B. Interior angles at A and C are 68° and 22° respectively.
spec.answerVisibility: All added labels and construction marks appear only in the answer.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the distance, to the nearest kilometre, between Checkpoint $A$ and Checkpoint $C$.

answer.worked:
Let $AC=x\text{ km}$. Relative to the $68^\circ$ angle at $A$, $AB$ is adjacent and $AC$ is the hypotenuse.
$$\begin{aligned}\cos68^\circ&=\frac{42}{x}\\x\cos68^\circ&=42\\x&=\frac{42}{\cos68^\circ}\\x&\approx112\text{ km}.\end{aligned}$$
Checkpoints $A$ and $C$ are 112 km apart, to the nearest kilometre.

children.label: c
children.prompt: If a runner is travelling $12.6\text{ km/h}$, how long does it take her to travel between Checkpoint $A$ and Checkpoint $B$, in hours and minutes?
